Definition: a fountain (also collectively), figuratively, a source (of satisfaction)
BiblicalUsage: The word names a fountain, a spring of water, and it runs from the flood to the gospel. In the days of Noah all the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and after the flood the fountains of the deep were stopped and the rain was restrained. Isaiah says with joy shall you draw water out of the wells of salvation, and Hosea warns that the east wind will dry up Ephraim's spring and his fountain shall be dried up.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the fountain is the Bible's picture of God's supply: He breaks it open in judgment and stops it in mercy, and He opens it again for joy. I hold that the wells of salvation never run dry, because the Fountain is God Himself, and those who draw from Him draw with joy.
